\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{\textquotedblleft{}he knew, he recognised\textquotedblright{} — one of Arabic's two words for knowing, whose root reached Spain and named a palace in Granada}\enspace\emph{\ar{عرف}}\enspace(ʿarafa)\par

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{\textquotedblleft{}he loved\textquotedblright{} — the chapter's payoff, closing the ladder of four verb shapes, and the root behind the ḥabībī of every second Arabic song}\enspace\emph{\ar{أحبّ}}\enspace(ʾaḥabba)\par

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}

\raggedright
\textbf{\textquotedblleft{}he said\textquotedblright{} — the letter qāf finally named, and one root that yields a saying, an article, a speaker and a spoken thing}\enspace\emph{\ar{قال}}\enspace(qāla)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: etymology; \hyperref[ch:ar-saying-and-seeing]{Chapter~29, p.~\pageref*{ch:ar-saying-and-seeing}}

\raggedright

\footnotesize explicit focus: etymology; \hyperref[ch:ar-saying-and-seeing]{Chapter~29, p.~\pageref*{ch:ar-saying-and-seeing}}

\raggedright
\textbf{\textquotedblleft{}he thought\textquotedblright{} — the first verb that is not a bare root at all, but a root rebuilt by doubling its middle letter, and the mu- doer that comes with the rebuild}\enspace\emph{\ar{فكّر}}\enspace(fakkara)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, etymology; \hyperref[ch:ar-taking-thinking-helping-loving]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:ar-taking-thinking-helping-loving}}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright

\footnotesize explicit focus: script, etymology; \hyperref[ch:ar-understanding-reading-writing]{Chapter~31, p.~\pageref*{ch:ar-understanding-reading-writing}}
